decisions.reason: Confirmed the counterexample directly: choose iid centered finite-variance innovations and an independent nonzero centered finite-variance C. Then X_t=mu+epsilon_t+C is weakly stationary and (1-B)(X-mu)=(1-B)epsilon, but X-mu!=epsilon. Thus cancelling 1-B discards solutions. The definition now imposes a normalized coprime equation and explicitly defines cancellation as an associated reduced model, without asserting solution-set equivalence.

Added that dependency and F6, then used the OLS full-vector normal limit and an explicit tail bound to prove all coefficient consistency; no projection limit is needed. The corollary Statement is unchanged.
